picks.excerpt: OpenAI unveiled its first hardware product - the $230 Codex Micro, a programmable macro pad made with Work Louder for its AI coding agent, with 13 mechanical switches, a touch sensor, rotary dial, and joystick.
picks.rationale: OpenAI's first shipping hardware and a genuinely new physical UI for driving AI coding agents - novel, on-bias, and directly changes how developers/designers wire up agent workflows.

picks.excerpt: Google Home is rolling out visual enhancements for weather and sports on smart displays, and Gemini's voice assistant now handles back-to-back commands more reliably without interrupting for voice verification.
picks.rationale: Concrete shipping update to ambient AI in the home - Gemini handling chained commands more fluidly is an on-bias signal of how assistant UX is maturing on smart displays.

picks.excerpt: Nothing's shipping $99 Ear (3a) earbuds add an on-device Audio Snapshot recorder - pinch to capture up to 60 seconds - with AI transcription, summaries and speaker ID in the Nothing X app, plus ChatGPT integration.
picks.rationale: New shipping product that bakes on-device capture, AI transcription/summaries and ChatGPT into $99 earbuds - a concrete, affordable example of ambient AI moving into everyday wearables.
